title: Meeting Rooms II
description:
Given an array of meeting time intervals `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i]`, return the minimum number of conference rooms required so that all meetings can take place.

A room vacated at time `t` can be immediately reused by another meeting starting at time `t` (i.e., intervals `[a, b]` and `[b, c]` do not overlap).
hints: Sort the meetings chronologically by start time so you allocate rooms in the order meetings begin.
Keep a min-heap storing the end times of all currently active meetings. The top of the heap is the room that frees up earliest.
When a new meeting starts at time s, if the earliest end time in the heap is <= s, pop it (reuse that room), then push the new meeting's end time.

examples.explanation: Meeting [0, 30] overlaps with [5, 10] and [15, 20], while [5, 10] and [15, 20] can share a room; 2 rooms are needed.
[2, 4] finishes before [7, 10] begins, so 1 room suffices.
Back-to-back meetings [1, 5], [5, 10], and [10, 15] touch at endpoints and can all reuse a single room.
